claims.text: The baseline material is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a homogeneous, single-phase solid-solution state without secondary precipitates.
Baseline CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low hardness.
Baseline CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low strength or yield strength.
The low hardness and strength arise because the homogeneous single-phase state provides little resistance to dislocation motion.
The baseline alloy readily activates multiple slip systems, including slip on {110} planes.
Facile multiple slip produces pronounced plasticity characterized by many small slips.
The absence of precipitate obstacles reduces the accumulation of strain-induced hardening.
The random distribution of constituent atoms in the solid solution minimizes lattice friction.
The random solid-solution state minimizes mechanical anisotropy.
A minor boron addition can induce intergranular or intragranular boride precipitation in CoCrFeNiTi.
The induced precipitates impede or pin dislocations.
Precipitate-induced obstruction and pileups increase strain hardening.
The precipitate-containing alloy will have higher hardness than baseline CoCrFeNiTi.
The precipitate-containing alloy will have higher yield strength than baseline CoCrFeNiTi.
At room temperature under quasi-static loading, deformation in the specified CoCrFeNiTi state is primarily governed by dislocation glide.

contradictions.description: The intervention requires successful precipitation to manipulate the proposed mediator, but the falsification rule treats failure to produce effective precipitation as falsification. Absence of precipitation would instead indicate a failed intervention and would not test whether precipitates strengthen the alloy.
